title: Two calls, one task: a loose paragraph vs a structured prompt

events.label: Pose the extraction task
events.detail: "Pull the key information out of this customer email." — the goal is structured fields that can enter a database, not a graceful retelling.

events.label: v1: a loose-paragraph prompt
events.detail: "Extract all the information from the email, be thorough." — no field list, no output format declared; everything is left to the model's improvisation.

events.label: v1 call
events.detail: Same model, same email, same parameters — the only difference between the two calls is the structure of the prompt.

events.label: v1 output: prose
events.detail: "The email is from Manager Zhang, who hopes the return can be handled soon, and mentions replying before next Wednesday…" — the facts are all there but scattered: the sender field is missing, the date is relative, priority is unstated.

events.label: v1 fails validation
events.detail: The database needs 4 fields (sender / deadline / priority / reply_by); the prose yields only 2 reliably parseable. The validator reports missing fields — the failure was baked into the prompt.

events.label: Debrief: the format was never declared
events.detail: The model never knew "there are 4 fields" — conversational inertia produced prose. When output format goes wrong, the root is usually an input without rules.

events.label: v2: the structured quartet
events.detail: Role ("You are the ticket-entry assistant") + task ("extract the following fields from the email") + constraints ("fill missing fields with null; dates in YYYY-MM-DD") + output format ("output JSON only, fields: sender, deadline, priority, reply_by").

events.label: v2 call
events.detail: The field list pins down the model's prose instinct — what to write and what shape it takes are both nailed down.

events.label: v2 output: JSON
events.detail: {"sender":"Manager Zhang","deadline":"2026-09-09","priority":"high","reply_by":"2026-09-08"} — all four fields, delivered in one pass.

events.label: v2 passes validation
events.detail: 4/4 fields present, types correct, dates compliant. Same model, same task — only the prompt's structure changed.

events.label: Deliver the structured result
events.detail: Downstream receives JSON ready for the database — the payoff of "saying what you mean" is determinism across the whole data pipeline.

events.label: Record the comparison
events.detail: The v1/v2 prompts and outputs are archived side by side. Know the cost too: over-constraining the format can make the model squeeze facts to fit — constrain up to "enough", no further.
